questions.text: According to the passage, why is the pressure on the goods trade deficit likely to escalate?

options.text: As oil, gems, and jewellery imports have fallen less than their exports.
As the government believes rising commodity prices will help trade tallies.
Because half of the 14 key segments of exports growing.
Due to to a $24.2 billion trade deficit.
Because 0.4% drop expected in services exports in August.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'As oil, gems, and jewellery imports have fallen less than their exports.'

Key Points

  • The first sentence of the second paragraph says "With global commodity prices rising around 12% from June levels to hit a 15-month high this month, the pressure on the goods trade deficit is likely to escalate, especially as oil, gems, and jewellery imports have fallen less than their exports so far in 2023-24''.
  • From the above sentence, we can say that according to the passage, the pressure on the goods trade deficit is likely to escalate as oil, gems, and jewellery imports have fallen less than their exports.
     

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

questions.text: What is the most suitable title for the passage?

options.text: Turkey in talks for alternative to India-Middle East trade corridor plan.
Canada indefinitely postpones trade mission to India amid tensions.
August’s foreign trade numbers are worrisome, yet hold some hope.
Rupee settles near an all-time closing low as trade deficit widens.
India’s goods exports increased for the seventh consecutive time.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'August’s foreign trade numbers are worrisome, yet hold some hope.'

Key Points

  • The first sentence of the first paragraph says "India’s goods exports shrank for the seventh consecutive time and the ninth time in 11 months this August, while imports surged to hit the highest level since March this year'', the second-last sentence of the second paragraph says "That engineering goods, which account for a quarter of India’s exports, clocked their first uptick after eight months in August, with half of the 14 key segments of exports growing — the best performance in nine months — is a welcome sign'' and the last sentence of the second paragraph concludes "India needs to do all it can to nurture precious green shoots and support exporters''.
  • From the above sentences, we can say that the most suitable title for the passage is ''August’s foreign trade numbers are worrisome, yet hold some hope''.
     

Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.

questions.text: Which word is the most similar in meaning to the word 'exacerbate' used in the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Aggravate.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Exacerbate' means To make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse. (बिगाड़ देना विशेषतः रोग या समस्‍या को)
    • Example: Interfering now would only exacerbate the situation.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Alleviate - To make something less strong or bad. (पीड़ा या कष्‍ट के प्रभाव को कम करना)
      • Example: The organization works to alleviate world hunger and disease.
    • Mitigate - To make something less serious, painful, unpleasant, etc. (किसी बात की गंभीरता, पीड़ा, अरोचकता आदि को कम कर देना)
      • Example: We have to figure out a way to mitigate the costs.
    • Ease - To make something less serious or severe. (राहत महसूस करना या पहुँचाना)
      • Example: City planners are looking for ways to ease traffic.
    • Aggravate - To make something worse or more serious. (स्थिति को बिगाड़ देना; बदतर करना या होना, अधिक गंभीर बनाना)
      • Example: Cigarettes can aggravate the symptoms of a cold.
    • Improve - To become or to make something better. (किसी स्थिति का बेहतर होना या उसे बेहतर बनाना, सुधरना या सुधारना)
      • Example: I hope the weather will improve later on.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 4.

Additional Information

  • The synonyms of the word 'Exacerbate' are "Aggravate, Worsen, Intensify".
  • The antonyms of the word 'Exacerbate' are "Alleviate, Mitigate, Ease".

questions.text: Which word is the most opposite in meaning to the word 'turmoil' used in the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Tranquillity.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Turmoil' means A disturbed or uneasy state. (खलबली या अनिश्‍चितता की स्थिति)
    • Example: The country is in a state of political turmoil.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Upheaval - A sudden big change, especially one that causes a lot of trouble. (एकाएक बड़ा परिवर्तन विशेषतः मुसीबतें पैदा करने वाला, उथल-पुथल, महापरिवर्तन)
      • Example: Yesterday's coup brought further upheaval to a country already struggling with famine.
    • Tranquillity - The quality or state of being tranquil; calm. (शांति, प्रशांति, शांत अवस्था)
      • Example: The island is a haven of peace and tranquillity.
    • Agitation - A state of anxiety or nervous excitement. (आंदोलन; उत्तेजना, अशांति)
      • Example: There has been mass agitation against the president.
    • Ferment - A state of political or social excitement and change. (राजनीतिक या सामाजिक उत्तेजना, अनिश्‍चय और परिवर्तन की स्थिति)
      • Example: The whole country was in a state of ferment.
    • Unrest - A state of dissatisfaction, disturbance, and agitation. (अशांति, असंतोष, उपद्रव)
      • Example: There is growing unrest throughout the country.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 2.

Additional Information

  • The antonyms of the word 'Turmoil' are "Tranquillity, Calm, Peace".
  • The synonyms of the word 'Turmoil' are "Upheaval, Agitation, Unrest".

questions.text: As per the passage, Services exports for last month will be known later, but Commerce Ministry extrapolations suggest that this engine which has been resilient so far through the global economic turmoil, is also _______.

questions.text: According to the passage, what led to a $24.2 billion trade deficit?

options.text: The pressure on the goods trade deficit.
The fall of exports by a relatively steeper 6.9%.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'The fall of exports by a relatively steeper 6.9%.'

Key Points

  • The second sentence of the first paragraph says "At $58.6 billion, inbound shipments were still 5.2% below last August’s levels, but exports fell by a relatively steeper 6.9%, leading to a $24.2 billion trade deficit — the widest since October 2022.''
  • From the above sentence, we can say that according to the passage, the fall of exports by a relatively steeper 6.9% led to a $24.2 billion trade deficit.
     

Hence, the only possible answer is option 5.

questions.text: What does the phrase ''good omen'' mean in the passage?

options.text: One shouldn’t settle on 'good enough' or take shortcuts.
Happiness is fleeting or that enjoyable experiences can’t last forever.
A sign, either real or imagined, of good fortune or a propitious outcome.
To confirm your approval of the idea or suggestion.
To express either irritation, frustration, dismay, anger or surprise.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'A sign, either real or imagined, of good fortune or a propitious outcome.'

Key Points

  • From the fifth sentence of the second paragraph, ''That is a good omen about demand for Indian goods amid the gloom, and the government believes rising commodity prices will help trade tallies'' we can interpret that there is good or propitious demand for Indian goods amid the gloom.
    • Example: I think the way our conversation ended is a good omen for where our relationship is headed.
  • From the above sentence, we can say that the phrase ''good omen'' means a sign, either real or imagined, of good fortune or a propitious outcome in the passage.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Important Points

  • ​Given below are the points, we should keep in mind while solving questions of reading comprehension:-
    • Identify the purpose of reading. 
    • Try to go through the question first then the passage so that you can just focus on the things you need to look at in the passage.
    • Anticipate what may lie ahead. 
    • Look out for specific information in the passage.
    • Read the passage quickly to get a general idea of meaning or to find specific information, e.g. figures or names.

questions.text:
Directions: In the sentence, certain words are in bold and numbered from A to E, which are the possible pairs to be interchanged. Choose the pair(s) of words that need to be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful. 

In times of (A) instinct, these are the kinds of decisions families are (B) confronted with when one or both parents are health care workers for whom the nature of their (C) courageous line of work means (D) balancing public service with the (E) crisis to look out for one’s own family.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e. A-E.

Key Points

Let us look at the sentence in the following way-

In times of (A) ______, these are the kinds of decisions families are (B)  ______ with when one or both parents are health care workers for whom the nature of their (C)  ______ line of work means (D)  ______ public service with the (E) ______to look out for one’s own family.

  • Meanings of the words given in bold are:
    • Instinct means a natural or intuitive way of acting or thinking.
    • Confronted means came face to face with (someone) with hostile or argumentative intent.
    • Courageous means not deterred by danger or pain; brave.
    • Balancing means counteracting or equaling the effect or importance of.
    • Crisis means a time of intense difficulty or danger.
  • It is clear that B and C are correct. Also, D justifies the bold word.
  • Clearly, we cannot say "in times of natural way of acting", but we can say "in times of difficulty and danger". To make the sentence meaningful, we need to interchange A and E.

Corrected sentence - "In times of crisis, these are the kinds of decisions families are confronted with when one or both parents are health care workers for whom the nature of their courageous line of work means balancing public service with the instinct to look out for one’s own family."

questions.text:
In the sentence, certain words are in bold and numbered from A to E, which are the possible pairs to be interchanged. Choose the pair(s) of words which need to be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.

Taking a sample of six (A) developing countries, reflecting a spread across the globe, the NGO (B) creates the burning of plastic packaging put on to the market by the companies (C) estimated 4.6m tonnes of carbon dioxide (D) equivalent to the (E) emissions from 2m cars.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Key Points

  • The word "creates" (B) is incorrectly placed. It refers to the act of producing or making something, which does not fit the current context.
  • The word "estimated" (C) should be swapped with "creates" (B) to make the sentence meaningful.
  • The correct placement would be "estimated" in place of "creates" and "creates" in place of "estimated" fitting into the sentence properly.
  • Thus, "creates" and "estimated" need to be interchanged to make the sentence coherent and meaningful.

Hence, the correct answer is 'B - C'.

Correct Sentence: Taking a sample of six developing countries, reflecting a spread across the globe, the NGO estimated the burning of plastic packaging put on to the market by the companies creates 4.6m tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent to the emissions from 2m cars.

Additional Information

  • Option 1: Interchanging "developing" (A) and "emissions" (E) would not make sense as they refer to entirely different concepts.
  • Option 3: Interchanging "creates" (B) and "developing (A) disrupts the sentence structure.
  • Option 4: Interchanging "developing" (A) and "estimated" (C) does not resolve the incorrect placement of "creates".
  • Option 5: No interchange required is incorrect because the current placement of "creates" (B) and "estimated" (C) does not make the sentence meaningful.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

We can look into the sentence in the following way-

(A) _________ into your (B) _________ mind can measure your IQ, identify your (C) _________ strengths and weaknesses, (D) _________ your personality and determine your (E)_________ for learning specific types of information.

  • Meanings of the words given in bold are:
    • Wandering means travelling aimlessly from place to place.
    • Tapping means exploiting or drawing a supply from (a resource).
    • Cognitive means relating to cognition.
    • Perceive means become aware or conscious of (something); come to realize or understand.
    • Aptitude means a natural ability to do something; talent.
  • It is clear that C and D are correct. Also, E justifies the bold word.
  • We need an adjective at B that can correctly describe the mind. At A, we require a verb. Wandering is an adjective and tapping is a verb. Hence, we need to interchange A and B to make the sentence correct.

Corrected sentence - (A) Tapping into your (B) wandering mind can measure your IQ, identify your (C) cognitive strengths and weaknesses, (D) perceive your personality and determine your (E) aptitude for learning specific types of information.

questions.text:

Additional Information

The duty of the (A) preach parent is plain: to save the child by any possible means, to (B) skeptical the uselessness of the (C) sacrifice in season and out of season, and to (D) endure patiently whatever penalty the law may (E) indict for evasion.

Direction: In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. The phrases are labeled A, B, and C in the first column and P, Q, and R in the second column. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase in the second column to make a grammatically and contextually meaningful sentence. Identify the correct option from those given below that gives the correct sequence in which one or more sentences can be formed. If none of the options makes it possible for a meaningful sentence to be formed, indicate 'None of these' as your answer.
 
Column 1
Column 2
(A) We pitched the tent
(P) copper and tin.
(B) Bronze is an alloy of
(Q) by a loud noise.
(C) The guards were alerted
(R) just beside the lake.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is B-P.
Key Points
The right combination from the given options that makes a meaningful sentence is B and P.
Let us take a look at the sentence combinations:
  • A is combined with R to form a meaningful sentence: We pitched the tent just beside the lake.
  • A cannot be used with either P or Q because it would not make a meaningful sentence.
    We pitched the tent copper and tin.
    We pitched the tent by a loud noise.

  • If we consider the combination B-Q, it does not make any meaningful sentence:
    Bronze is an alloy of by a loud noise.
  • Then, the final combination is C-Q: The guards were alerted by a loud noise.
     
Thus, the correct combination of sentences from the given options is: (B) Bronze is an alloy of (P) copper and tin.

questions.text:
Which of the phrases given below the sentence should replace the word/phrase that is given in bold in the sentence to make it grammatically correct? If the sentence is correct as it is given and no correction is required, mark 'No correction required' as the answer.

Either I will opt for Commerce or opt for Arts after my board examination is over.

options.text: I will neither opt for Commerce or for Arts
I will either opt for Commerce or opt for Arts
I will either opt for Commerce nor for Arts
Either I will opt for Commerce or Arts

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is I will either opt for Commerce or opt for Arts.
Key Points
The correct format for either...or is: I + be verb + either + _______ + or + ________.
  • For example: I am either studying or staying home.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is: I will either opt for Commerce or opt for Arts after my board examination is over.
​Mistake Points
 
When helping verbs (am, is, are, was, were, has, have, had, will, would, should etc) connect two verbs or verb phrases, the helping verb is not repeated after “or”. For example:
  • He will either come here or will stay at the station. (incorrect)
  • He will either come here or stay at the station. (correct)

  • ​Therefore, the correct answer is: He is oblivious of the cut-throat competition and thinks that life is a bed of roses.

Word Meaning

Cause of result from

Certain of assured

Upon not receiving the package, I asked the delivery person, "Whom did you deliver the package to?"

Key Points

  • Using "whom" adheres to formal grammatical rules.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 5: No correction required.
 
Correct Sentence: "Upon not receiving the package, I asked the delivery person, 'Whom did you deliver the package to?'"
 
Additional Information

  • Option 2: "Who the package was delivered?" is grammatically incorrect.
  • Option 4: "Which did you deliver the package to?" is grammatically incorrect and does not make sense.
  • No correction required is appropriate here considering the formality required.

questions.text: Choose the correct word to fill the 1st blank.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is “dazzling”.

Key Points

The passage begins by mentioning the pockets of methane that are tapped within Canada’s frozen lake. They are described as a natural wonder. Further, looking at that part of the sentence with the 1st blank, it is followed by the conjunction ‘yet’ which is usually used to show contrast.

Turnaround time is not the optimum criterion in an interactive system. The interval from the time of submission of a process to the time of completion. It is the sum of the periods spent waiting to get into memory, waiting in the ready queue, executing on the CPU, and doing I/O.

questions.text: In which of the following states the transaction executes all its operations successfully and all the effects are now permanently saved on the database system?

options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Committed

  • Active state: The active state is the first state of every transaction. In this state, the transaction is being executed.
  • Partially committed: In the partially committed state, a transaction executes its final operation, but the data is still not saved to the database.
  • Committed: A transaction is said to be in a committed state if it executes all its operations successfully. In this state, all the effects are now permanently saved on the database system.
  • Failed state: If any of the checks made by the database recovery system fails, then the transaction is said to be in the failed state.
  • Aborted: If any of the checks fail and the transaction has reached a failed state then the database recovery system will make sure that the database is in its previous consistent state. If not, then it will abort or roll back the transaction to bring the database into a consistent state.
  • If the transaction fails in the middle of the transaction then before executing the transaction, all the executed transactions are rolled back to its consistent state. After aborting the transaction, the database recovery module will select one of the two operations:
    • Re-start the transaction
    • Kill the transaction

questions.text: _________ is used to prevent unauthorized interceptors from accessing telecommunications.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Link encryption

  • In the data link layer, packets on a point-to-point line can be encrypted as they leave one machine and decrypted as they enter another.
  • The packet breaks down when packets must traverse multiple routers, however, because packets must be decrypted at each router, leaving them vulnerable to attacks from within the router
  • Link encryption is the method used to prevent this security issue
  • The two main kinds of encryption are symmetric encryption and asymmetric encryption. Asymmetric encryption is also known as public-key encryption.
    • In symmetric encryption, there is only one key, and all communicating parties use the same key for encryption and decryption.
    • In asymmetric, or public key, encryption, there are two keys: one key is used for encryption, and a different key is used for decryption. Either key can be used for either action, but data encrypted with the first key can only be decrypted with the second key, and vice versa. One key is kept private, while one key is shared publicly, for anyone to use – hence the "public key" name. Asymmetric encryption is a foundational technology for SSL (TLS).

questions.text: Which of the following parameter passing mechanism(s) is/are supported by C++, but not by C?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Concept:

Pass by reference:

Pass-by-reference means to pass the reference of an argument in the calling function to the corresponding formal parameter of the called function.

Pass by value:

Pass by value means that a copy of the actual parameter's value is made in memory, i.e. the caller and callee have two independent variables with the same value. If the callee modifies the parameter value, the effect is not visible to the caller.

Explanation:

C does not support implicitly passing a variable by reference. We need to explicitly create a reference (with & ) before calling the function and explicitly dereference it (with * ) in the function. So there is no pass-by-reference in C.

Hence the correct answer is Pass by reference.
